messages.content: Predict the participant’s actual response in an anonymous number-selection experiment on Amazon Mechanical Turk. There are three players in a group. Each independently chooses a WHOLE number from 1 to 50. Let m be the lowest of the three numbers and k be the number of players tied at m. Each player who chose m earns m/k experimental points; all other players earn zero. For example, choices 44,44,50 give 22 points to each player choosing 44 and zero to the player choosing 50. A point is worth USD 0.03, in addition to the fixed USD 1 participation fee. Players answer separately in their own time; groups and outcomes are determined after everyone has responded. Players do not learn the identities, current choices or earnings of the others before responding. This person is now making the number choice for the first game. Return only the whole number 1–50 that they choose, not their points or an optimal strategy.

The participant is 33 years old. They reported gender Male. Before the real game they answered two rule questions. For own28, other28 and36, their stated own earnings were 14 points. For own38, other45 and14, their stated own earnings were 0 points. These are their prior answers. What whole number 1–50 does this person choose for the first game?

Predict the participant’s actual response in an anonymous number-selection experiment on Amazon Mechanical Turk. There are three players in a group. Each independently chooses a WHOLE number from 1 to 50. Let m be the lowest of the three numbers and k be the number of players tied at m. Each player who chose m earns m/k experimental points; all other players earn zero. For example, choices 44,44,50 give 22 points to each player choosing 44 and zero to the player choosing 50. A point is worth USD 0.03, in addition to the fixed USD 1 participation fee. Players answer separately in their own time; groups and outcomes are determined after everyone has responded. Players do not learn the identities, current choices or earnings of the others before responding. This person has already chosen their own number. They are NOW asked to estimate the average number chosen by the OTHER TWO members of this group, excluding their own number. An estimate earns an extra USD 0.25 if it differs from the actual two-person average by at most 5 in either direction. No other choices or game outcome have been revealed. Predict their subjective numerical estimate; return only that number, not their own earlier number or an actual calculated average.

The participant is 33 years old. They reported gender Male. Before the real game they answered two rule questions. For own28, other28 and36, their stated own earnings were 14 points. For own38, other45 and14, their stated own earnings were 0 points. These are their prior answers. Their number chosen in the first game was 1. What average number does this person estimate for the other two players in the first group?

Predict the participant’s actual response in an anonymous number-selection experiment on Amazon Mechanical Turk. There are three players in a group. Each independently chooses a WHOLE number from 1 to 50. Let m be the lowest of the three numbers and k be the number of players tied at m. Each player who chose m earns m/k experimental points; all other players earn zero. For example, choices 44,44,50 give 22 points to each player choosing 44 and zero to the player choosing 50. A point is worth USD 0.03, in addition to the fixed USD 1 participation fee. Players answer separately in their own time; groups and outcomes are determined after everyone has responded. Players do not learn the identities, current choices or earnings of the others before responding. The first game and its estimate are completed, with no outcome feedback. This is the SECOND and final game, with two entirely different other players. Before outcomes are determined each player reports a vote and a planned number for EACH of two possible group decisions. An agreement exists if at least two of the three vote For it. It is a collective promise that everyone will choose 50, but it is NON-BINDING: every player may still choose any whole number 1–50. With an agreement there is a 20% chance, determined after decisions, that this second game’s results do not count and everyone in that group earns zero points from it. Without an agreement there is no such cancellation risk. The group’s actual votes and outcome have not been revealed. Each player states a number for each possible group decision; afterward the actual group vote determines which conditional number is used. Predict this person’s vote: For means in favour of making this agreement; Against means opposed. Return only For or Against.

Each independently chooses a WHOLE number from 1 to 50. Let m be the lowest of the three numbers and k be the number of players tied at m. Each player who chose m earns m/k experimental points; all other players earn zero. For example, choices 44,44,50 give 22 points to each player choosing 44 and zero to the player choosing 50. A point is worth USD 0.03, in addition to the fixed USD 1 participation fee. Players answer separately in their own time; groups and outcomes are determined after everyone has responded. Players do not learn the identities, current choices or earnings of the others before responding. The first game and its estimate are completed, with no outcome feedback. This is the SECOND and final game, with two entirely different other players. Before outcomes are determined each player reports a vote and a planned number for EACH of two possible group decisions. An agreement exists if at least two of the three vote For it. It is a collective promise that everyone will choose 50, but it is NON-BINDING: every player may still choose any whole number 1–50. With an agreement there is a 20% chance, determined after decisions, that this second game’s results do not count and everyone in that group earns zero points from it. Without an agreement there is no such cancellation risk. The group’s actual votes and outcome have not been revealed. Each player states a number for each possible group decision; afterward the actual group vote determines which conditional number is used. Predict the person’s planned whole number for the specified conditional case. Return only an integer 1–50, not a vote or earnings.

The participant is 30 years old. They reported gender Male. Before the real game they answered two rule questions. For own28, other28 and36, their stated own earnings were 14 points. For own38, other45 and14, their stated own earnings were 19 points. These are their prior answers. Their number chosen in the first game was 25. Their subsequent estimate for the OTHER TWO first-game players’ mean was 18. Neither first-game outcomes nor the other players’ choices have been disclosed. Give their planned number for the case where the second group DECIDES TO HAVE the agreement to choose 50. This is a conditional report; the actual group vote is not known.
